question: A 22-year-old student presents with headaches occurring after 2–3 hours of reading, relieved by rest, associated with mild eye strain. Vision is 6/6 unaided. Which finding would MOST strongly indicate referral beyond simple refraction?

answers.text: Headache onset at the end of the working day

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: End-of-day headaches after sustained near-work are classic asthenopia from accommodative fatigue. This does not itself mandate urgent referral.
Correct. Papilloedema is a sign of raised intracranial pressure and mandates immediate neurology/neurosurgery referral regardless of refractive status. It is never caused by refractive error.
Low hypermetropia is a well-recognised cause of asthenopic headache due to sustained accommodative effort. Spectacle correction usually resolves symptoms.
Small print increases accommodative demand and is an expected aggravating factor in refractive headache. This is not a red flag for sinister pathology.

overallFeedback.feedback: Red flags that mandate referral beyond refraction: papilloedema, visual field defects, afferent pupillary defect, symptoms waking from sleep, associated vomiting. Always examine the fundus.
Correct. Papilloedema = raised ICP = urgent referral. No refractive cause produces disc swelling.
